chapter: Radio, theaters and early dance forms
title: Ragtime, quadrilles and lancers
summary: DeDroit recalls playing rags and old dances at Odd Fellows Hall with a band that stood up to play.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: It sounds funny, but that's it. How about ragtime music? Do you remember

it? Oh, I played plenty of ragtime music. At the same time you're playing? I'll tell you what we used to do. We'd play a dance. Like I tell you, there was a place called the Oddfellas Hall. They had a hard one. And we'd play numbers like the eccentric rag or Empire Rag or something like that. And we'd get up with the trumpets and we'd play it over the railing. All the way to make a lot of notes, like Down Home Rag. Remember the Down Home Rag? Yeah. That was a good number to show off to trumpet guys, doesn't it? We'd have three trumpets, two altos, pick-horns, a baritone tuba, and two drums. One guy played a bass drum. And we made good bands. We played shottishes, we played lances, we played varieties. You ever hear of those?
I haven't heard of varieties. I've heard of the other ones. You heard of lances? Oh yes.

We'd make a roll and now we'll have a lances. They formed their groups. You know how they do it. They go in and out. It's more like the square dancing and round dancing that you see today, see? And the fact that we'd stand up and play, it was a little different. My father used to give the trombone play a dollar extra every time we played tromboneum. There's a number called tromboneum. You know we didn't make a lot of money in those days. The scale was fine. Some guys would cheat and play for fours.
